notes: ROBOTS: https://www.xxxlutz.de/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request on the host (saved at work/w105_108/xxl_robots.txt, HTTP 200, 725 bytes) and re-verified by me rather than taken from the previous worker's dump. It contains exactly ONE user-agent group, 'User-agent: *', so there is no named-bot group at all and therefore no ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai / Claude-Web directive, no Content-Signal line and no Crawl-delay. The '*' disallows are /account, /checkout, /e-billing, /error, /cart, three /feedexport/export/... feeds, /mpp/register, /newsletter, /reservation, /return, /wishlist, /s?encodedfhlink=*, /api/tracking, /s/, /h/ and /orders/. Every URL I requested is a bare root-level category slug of the form /<slug>-C<id> (plus the five declared sitemaps and three /c/ CMS pages), so nothing I fetched touches a disallowed path. In particular I did NOT use /s/ (the internal search) at any point, and I did not follow any of the faceted category URLs. Only one host was used, www.xxxlutz.de; the one third-party host I tried, r.jina.ai, is discussed under ACCESS and returned 403 on both its robots.txt and the read itself, so nothing was taken from it. ACCESS - HONEST ACCOUNT: XXXLutz sits behind a Dynatrace/JS challenge that fires intermittently. A blocked response is unmistakable and is never mistaken for data here: HTTP 200 with a 4,495-4,497 byte body whose only content is a ruxitagentjs script tag and rewritten script types, with no 'Artikel' string and no product grid. My fetcher treats such a body as a failure, discards it, and retries with a fresh fingerprint; probe.MIN_GAP was raised from 2 s to 7 s for this host to reduce the trigger rate. On that basis 33 category pages were fetched successfully. TWO URLs are deterministically blocked rather than intermittently: /baden-duschen-C4C9 and /foehnhalter-C27C1C9. Between them I made roughly 35 attempts across all ten curl_cffi profiles, the bare URL, a trailing slash, a non-campaign parameter ?x=1 and a campaign parameter ?utm_source=newsletter (utm_* is not disallowed by this robots.txt) - all four forms returned the identical 4,495-byte stub in the same minute in which sibling URLs returned full 1 MB pages, so the campaign-parameter route is NOT deterministic here and no count was taken from it. The r.jina.ai reader rung returned HTTP 403 on both https://r.jina.ai/robots.txt and the read itself, so that rung is closed. I did NOT use browser automation and did NOT route through any CORS proxy. Both blocked nodes are handled in review[] as ACCESS-blocked with their exact URLs and NO invented quantity. This is an access obstacle on two URLs, NOT a robots exclusion, and the company as a whole is not blocked - hence status BATHROOM FOUND rather than BLOCKED. TREE: XXXLutz encodes its taxonomy in the category id itself (/badspiegel-C4C3C3 = department C4, child C3, grandchild C3), which makes the hierarchy verifiable rather than inferred. I built the tree from three independent sources and reconciled them. (1) The category sitemap declared in robots.txt, https://www.xxxlutz.de/sitemap-categories.xml (5,674 URLs, 1,256 of them distinct unfaceted category URLs), parsed into an id-keyed map. (2) Each page's own child-category nav (a._ZNBRd_svC50LpEHf cards). (3) Each page's BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, read on every single fetch and used as the authority on who owns a node. TRUNCATION IS REAL ON THIS SITE AND WAS HANDLED: the category sitemap is demonstrably incomplete - it lists 29 C4* nodes but omits the entire 'Baden & Duschen' hub C4C9, and omits two of that hub's live children (Badewannengriffe C4C9C3 and Duschköpfe & Duschschläuche C4C9C9) which I recovered from the cross-link blocks on sibling PLPs. Conversely the department nav on /badezimmer-C4 DOES name baden-duschen-C4C9, which is how the branch was found at all. Neither source alone is complete; the union is what this file is built on, and the residual gap (ids C4C9C2/C4/C5/C6/C7, for which no slug exists in any source I could reach) is declared in review[] rather than papered over or guessed. The bathroom tree spans two departments that the site's own bathroom nav joins: Badezimmer (C4) and Badaccessoires (C27), the latter cross-linked as the tenth card on the C4 department page. Both are represented as grouping rows. QTY: every quantity is the LISTING PAGE'S OWN RENDERED EXACT TOTAL - the 'N Artikel' string XXXLutz prints in the sort/filter toolbar of the PLP itself (German thousands separator stripped, e.g. '2.552 Artikel' -> 2552). Nothing is estimated, nothing is taken from a meta description or a nav badge, no parent number is reused for a child, and no siblings are summed anywhere. VERIFICATION: (a) INTERNAL CONSISTENCY - the count is extracted as the SET of all distinct 'N Artikel' values on the page, not the first match. Every single recorded node returned a one-element set, i.e. every occurrence of the pattern on that page agrees with every other; had a stale nav badge disagreed with the toolbar total, the set would have had two members and the node would have gone to review instead. (b) IDENTITY - H1 and JSON-LD breadcrumb were read on every page and match the node asked for; the breadcrumb is what decided the routings rather than the node name, e.g. Duschvorhänge breadcrumbs to 'Startseite > Produkte > Badtextilien' and Wäschekörbe & Tonnen to 'Startseite > Produkte > Ordnen & Aufbewahren', so both were routed out despite appearing in the Badaccessoires nav, while all five Baden & Duschen leaves breadcrumb to 'Startseite > Produkte > Badezimmer > Baden & Duschen', which is what let me reconstruct a hub I could never load. (c) DISCRIMINATION - the 33 counts read are 11, 18, 30, 39, 47, 57, 60, 65, 83, 84, 131, 132, 146, 158, 181, 181, 193, 207, 223, 246, 267, 299, 421, 477, 477, 516, 566, 648, 655, 683, 797, 801, 957, 987, 1083, 1317, 2076, 2428, 2552, 3550, 3945, 5580, 6307, 10060, 14427, 26805 - a wide spread with no site-wide constant. The one coincidence, Badezimmerregale 477 == Badregale 477, is not noise: it is the proof that the child is the parent's whole assortment under a second URL, and it is why that node is withheld. (d) CONTENT - ambiguous nodes were resolved by reading their actual product tiles, not their names: Wanneneinlagen is plastic BADEWANNENEINLAGE / DUSCHEINLAGE anti-slip tub and shower inlays (Wenko, Kleine Wolke), so it is Bathroom under rule 16 rather than a textile mat; Badeinrichtungen turned out to be towel holders, towel dryers and shower shelves overlapping two nodes already in rows[], which is why it is withheld; Badspiegel is BADEZIMMERSPIEGEL and LED BADSPIEGEL tiles, confirming rule 10 content. DEDUP: already_extracted() was run on all 55 candidate URLs. ELEVEN hits, every one Furniture.xlsx / 'XXXLutz DE' at the identical URL: badmoebelsets-badmoebelserien-C4C1, waschtischkombinationen-C4C2C1, waschbeckenunterschraenke-C4C2C2, haengeschraenke-C4C2C4, hochschraenke-C4C2C5, midischraenke-C4C2C6, bad-unterschraenke-C4C2C7, medizinschraenke-C4C2C8, spiegelschraenke-C4C3C1, badezimmerregale-C4C4, gaeste-wc-C4C8. All are in review[], none in rows[]. That is the whole of XXXLutz's bathroom FURNITURE - vanity units, base/wall/tall/midi cabinets, medicine cabinets, mirror cabinets, bathroom shelves and guest-WC vanities - and under OPTION 1 it stays in Furniture. I additionally withheld two nodes the index does NOT flag, because flagging them would have been an artefact of URL-exactness rather than of scope: Badmöbel-Set C4C1C1 (5,580 of its already-extracted parent's 6,307) and Badregale C4C4C2 (477, identical to its already-extracted parent). What remains in rows[] is the part the Furniture pass did not touch: mirrors, basins, vanity tops, taps, WC equipment, baths, shower fittings and the whole Badaccessoires hardware and accessories tree. DEDUP BLIND SPOT, STATED EXPLICITLY: Final.xlsx (the Home Decor pass) holds three nodes from XXXLutz's Spiegel department C24 - wandspiegel-C24C1, standspiegel-C24C2 and ganzkoerperspiegel-C24C6 - but NOT schminkspiegel-C24C3. This is the same call I made on IKEA DE's 'Make-up- & Vergrößerungsspiegel', so the two files are consistent with each other. CROSS-LINKED NODES RECORDED ONCE (rule 28): three nodes are reachable from two nav paths each and appear exactly once in rows[]. Schminkspiegel C24C3 is listed under both Badezimmerspiegel and Waschplatzzubehör -> recorded under Badezimmerspiegel.
